weekend_summary: At the revived Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, Max Verstappen took pole (1:35.130) and won ahead of Kimi Antonelli and Lewis Hamilton. A major pre-race downpour delayed the start and created an intermediate-to-slick crossover. Verstappen lost the lead at the start but recovered; Ferrari recovered from an early slick-tyre disadvantage; George Russell retired late with a power-unit issue. The mixed-weather race classification is useful for result and strategy analysis but its pooled race-pace fingerprints are excluded from future normal dry-race prediction weighting.

Q.summary: Verstappen pole in 1:35.130, Hamilton P2 (+0.298s), Hadjar P3 before grid penalty, Antonelli P4, Leclerc P5.

key_moments.text: Verstappen topped all three phases of qualifying, taking pole in 1:35.130.
Hadjar qualified third but was demoted five places for power-unit parts; Colapinto and Lindblad also carried grid penalties.

R.summary: Verstappen won a rain-delayed mixed-weather race over Antonelli (+2.307s) and Hamilton (+4.919s).

key_moments.text: Rain delayed the start and teams split between slicks and intermediates.
Early Safety Car gave intermediate starters a favourable crossover to slicks; Ferrari recovered after starting on slicks.
Russell retired near the end with a power-unit problem; Verstappen won ahead of Antonelli and Hamilton.

VER.name: Max Verstappen

ANT.name: Kimi Antonelli
ANT.summary: Qualified fourth and finished second, extending the championship lead as Russell retired.

RUS.name: George Russell
RUS.summary: Qualified eighth, ran near the front after the start, but retired late due to a power-unit issue.

details.text: Race retirement was mechanical rather than a reliable pace indicator.

HAM.name: Lewis Hamilton
HAM.summary: Qualified second; an early slick-tyre gamble backfired before a recovery to third.

details.text: Ferrari lost track position on slicks at the wet start then recovered as the circuit dried.

HAD.name: Isack Hadjar
HAD.summary: Qualified third on pace but started further back after an engine-component penalty and finished fifth.

details.text: Qualifying pace and final grid slot must not be conflated.

Red Bull.summary: First Red Bull/Red Bull Ford victory of 2026 through Verstappen.

details.text: Pole and win demonstrated competitiveness, but wet-race finishing order is not a dry-pace benchmark.

Mercedes.summary: Introduced a substantial floor/rear-corner package; Antonelli finished second and Russell retired.

details.text: No isolated causal lap-time gain is asserted for the package.

Ferrari.summary: Hamilton and Leclerc finished third/fourth after a difficult opening tyre choice.

details.text: Intermediate-to-slick crossover timing dominated race-position changes.

strategy_and_conditions.text: Mixed wet/drying surface at the start, with early Safety Car and crossover to slicks; this was not a representative single-condition dry race.
Race-session classification is retained for outcomes, but R16 R is ineligible as future dry-race pace training evidence.
Grid penalties affected Hadjar, Colapinto and Lindblad; forecast pace ordering is not the final grid.

performance_interpretation.text: Verstappen was fastest in dry qualifying; qualifying and wet/mixed race results must be interpreted with different evidentiary weight.
The wet/dry crossover, Safety Car timing and tyre selection confound per-lap comparability.
